definitions.explanation: A general term for anything worn on the feet, including shoes, sandals, slippers, and traditional Japanese footwear such as geta and zori.

examples.japanese: {履物|はきもの}を{脱|ぬ}いでください。
{玄関|げんかん}に{履物|はきもの}がたくさん{並|なら}んでいる。
examples.english: A lot of footwear is lined up in the entryway.

examples.japanese: この{旅館|りょかん}では{館内用|かんないよう}の{履物|はきもの}が{用意|ようい}されている。
examples.english: This ryokan provides indoor footwear for guests.

notes:
A broad category word covering all types of footwear. More common in formal signs, traditional settings, and written instructions than in casual speech, where {靴|くつ} (shoes) is the default.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {履物|はきもの}を{脱|ぬ}ぐ (to take off footwear)
- {履物|はきもの}を{揃|そろ}える (to line up footwear neatly)
- {履物|はきもの}{禁止|きんし} (no footwear allowed)

USAGE:
Often seen on signs at temples, schools, and traditional buildings where shoes must be removed. While {靴|くつ} refers specifically to Western-style shoes, {履物|はきもの} encompasses everything from {下駄|げた} and {草履|ぞうり} to modern sneakers.
